## Summary
This postmortem covers a minor service degradation in auth-service that began at 10:12 UTC on October 27, 2025 and affected all traffic routed through the affected region.

## Root Cause
A deploy to auth-service at 10:12 UTC introduced a change to the checkout pricing calculation. The change passed CI but the test suite did not reproduce the production traffic shape, and the regression only became visible once real user traffic hit the new code path.

## Detection & Response
Automated monitoring fired 4 minutes into the incident on CPU utilization. The on-call engineer acknowledged in 8 minutes; initial triage was complicated by a wave of correlated alerts from downstream services before the team traced the issue back to auth-service.

## Resolution
The team mitigated impact by rolling back deploy DEP-01178, which brought error rates back to baseline within 11 minutes of the mitigation being applied. Full resolution, including validation that downstream services had recovered, was confirmed 23 minutes after the incident began.

## Contributing Factors
- no automated rollback trigger on error-rate regression
- insufficient canary analysis before full rollout

## Preventive Action
Extend the canary stage to a minimum of 30 minutes with automated error-budget gating.
